widgetTool.name: show_compare_table_card
widgetTool.description: Shows a small comparison table on chat: up to four columns and six rows, with one column optionally highlighted. Use it to compare payment plans side by side or this month with last month. Chat only; never on voice. Cells are display strings with money already formatted. Facts come only from tool results. No spoken pacing is needed. Call shape: name is always cx-show-compare-table-card and all card fields go inside payload.

name.description: Always exactly cx-show-compare-table-card (the card element this tool renders).

action_label.description: Optional button label under the table.

action_message.description: What the button sends as the customer's next message.

caption.description: Optional one short line under the table.

columns.description: Column headings, up to four, for example Monthly and Down payment.

display_text.description: Optional. The short on-screen text of the reply: the headline the table answers and one short question, in the customer's language. The website shows it instead of the long spoken text. Dollar amounts and dates are written in bold markdown (**$12.50**, **November 7, 2026**). The card never repeats this text.

highlight_column.description: Optional zero-based index of the column to highlight.

highlight_label.description: Optional tiny tag above the highlighted column heading.

cells.description: One display string per column, in column order.

note.description: Optional tiny line under the row name.

title.description: Heading, for example Payment plans for [amount] past due.

payload.description: The card data. Put every card field inside this object.

textResponseConfig.textResponseInstruction: Write this text as the full spoken explanation, exactly as a person would say it on a phone call: plain natural spoken sentences, built only from the tool results and nothing invented, that say every fact the card shows once (the card is never repeated afterwards). Say every amount, percentage and date in words (for example forty-one dollars and one cent, the twenty-sixth of October), never digits, dollar signs or symbols, and say a year in words too (twenty twenty-six); a confirmation or claim number is the one exception and is read as returned in short groups. Use no emoji, markdown, bullets, tables, symbols or line breaks, because the voice may read this text aloud. Say the headline the table answers, then every row for every column (the plan or month, then each of its figures, for example six months at a monthly amount with a down payment or none), any row note (such as the plan that needs energy assistance), the highlighted column and the caption, and end with the one short question the step asks. The short on-screen text goes only in display_text of the card payload (always pass it, written in the customer's language; digits and symbols are allowed there): one short sentence with the headline the table answers and one short question, with at most one emoji at the start only in a calm moment and never for hardship, past due, a shutoff, a complaint or an error. This text is the whole reply, so write no other text and no separate pacing sentence. When the tool call failed there is no card and the text stays short.
